title: Count Inversions
statement: Return the number of pairs (i, j) with i < j and nums[i] > nums[j]. An inversion is a pair that is out of sorted order.
hints: A double loop counts pairs and is quadratic.
Merge sort counts them while merging. When the right half contributes a value first, it is smaller than every remaining left value.
Add the number of remaining left values at that moment.

approaches.name: Modified merge sort
approaches.explanation: Inversions are split across the two halves plus the merge.

editorial: Inversions are of three kinds: inside the left half, inside the right half, and across the midpoint. The recursive calls count the first two. During the merge, every time a right value is taken before leftover left values, it forms an inversion with each of them. Sum those counts. The sorted merge is what makes the leftover left values a contiguous suffix.
reference_solution:
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
from collections import Counter, OrderedDict, defaultdict, deque
import heapq

def count_inversions(nums: list[int]) -> int:
    temp = nums[:]
    def sort_count(left: int, right: int) -> int:
        if right - left <= 1:
            return 0
        mid = (left + right) // 2
        inversions = sort_count(left, mid) + sort_count(mid, right)
        merged = []
        i, j = left, mid
        while i < mid and j < right:
            if temp[i] <= temp[j]:
                merged.append(temp[i])
                i += 1
            else:
                merged.append(temp[j])
                inversions += mid - i
                j += 1
        merged.extend(temp[i:mid])
        merged.extend(temp[j:right])
        temp[left:right] = merged
        return inversions

    return sort_count(0, len(temp))
